title: Metrics fanout router and SLI derivation for inference KPIs
creator: Lina Zhang
description:
Goal:
Deliver a robust, low-latency metrics collection pipeline for inference-specific KPIs that supports Prometheus remote_write, OpenTelemetry ingestion, and an internal fanout for SLI/SLO derivation. The pipeline must preserve high-cardinality data for debug traces while synthesizing low-cardinality SLIs for dashboards and alerts to avoid cardinality explosions and reduce storage costs.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: instrumenting runtime call sites with the new tracing hooks to emit lightweight OTLP metrics, introducing a metrics-fanout-router service (stateless), extending the OTel Collector config to route to Prometheus remote_write and Kafka for downstream enrichment, aggregation jobs for latency histograms and token-level KPIs, and dashboard/alert updates.
- Out of scope: full rework of model labeling strategy, long-term archival format changes, and RBAC changes for console viewing (handled in separate tickets).

Design summary:
1) Instrumentation: add a small metrics client carrying two emission modes: "hot" (high-cardinality debug metrics) and "sum" (pre-aggregated counters/histograms). Instrumentation will attach a minimal label set by default (model_id, route, region, tier) with the option to opt-in additional debug tags.
2) Sidecar vs. central ingestion: implement a light sidecar that forwards OTLP/Prometheus scrape exports to the metrics-fanout-router. To reduce duplicated work, SDKs will prefer pushing to a local UDP buffer then flush to sidecar; sidecars maintain per-pod batching windows.
3) Fanout router: a horizontally scalable stateless router that accepts OTLP and Prometheus remote_write, tags and normalizes metrics, applies rate-limiting and cardinality sampling rules, and writes to two sinks in parallel:
   - Prometheus remote_write (downsampled and low-cardinality set)
   - Kafka topic (metrics-enriched-v2) for SLI derivation and long-form retention
4) Aggregation/Derivation: a separate SLI worker consumes Kafka, computes per-model/service percentiles (p50,p90,p95,p99) from histogram buckets, and emits derived low-cardinality metrics to a dedicated Prometheus remote_write instance for dashboards/alerts.
5) Storage & retention: raw high-card metrics kept for 7d in Kafka/long-term store; derived SLIs retained for 90d in Prometheus long-term metrics backend.

Telemetry contract changes (backwards compatible):
- Metric names: inference.request.latency_ms (histogram), inference.request.errors (counter), inference.tokens.generated (counter).
- Required labels: model_id (string), route (string), region (string). Optional debug_label (string) allowed but will be sampled at ingestion.

Cardinality controls and sampling strategy:
- Static denylist for user-provided freeform tags.
- Token sampling: only 1% of requests include full client metadata; others include minimal label set.
- Hot-path debug captures are forwarded to Kafka under a separate topic with TTL and strict retention.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy sidecar + fanout-router to a single region and route 5% of traffic (internal infra and a single small customer). Collect differences between current Prometheus pipeline and new derived SLIs.
- Phase 2 (gradual increase): expand to 25% traffic with automated rollback triggers if p99 latency or ingestion error spikes > 10%.
- Phase 3 (cutover): full traffic switch and deprecation of legacy direct-prometheus pipeline.

Dashboards and alerts:
- New Grafana dashboards: "Per-model latency percentiles", "Per-tenant error rate (5m/1h)", "Prometheus ingestion success rate".
- Alert rules: SLO breach alert when derived error_rate > threshold for 5m, ingestion lag > 30s, and Kafka consumer lag > 10000 messages.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Keeping raw high-cardinality metrics vs storage cost: decided to retain 7d raw and export derived SLIs to cheaper long-term store.
- Sidecar complexity vs central collector: sidecar reduces cross-AZ traffic but requires lifecycle management; scoped to per-pod lightweight container to simplify upgrades.
- Histogram bucket schema: using adaptive buckets tuned per-model based on typical latency distribution; requires per-model profiling (follow-up ticket).

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Instrumentation changes in runtime (ENG runtime team): add hot/sum emission mode, ensure nonblocking emission, unit tests.
- Sidecar: implement batching, local buffer, and OTLP/remote_write adapter.
- Fanout router service: endpoint, normalization, cardinality rules, sink adapters.
- Kafka topic & consumer: topic config, SLI derivation job, consumer autoscaling.
- OTel Collector changes: new pipelines and exporters, test harness.
- Dashboards & alerts: Grafana panels, alert rules, runbooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- New pipeline can handle equivalent throughput to legacy path with <5% added tail latency on request path.
- Derived SLI metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and error rate) match sampled ground truth within 2% for p50/p90 and within 5% for p99 in A/B canary runs.
- No increase in customer-facing error rates during rollout (rollout safety gates in place).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: cardinality blow-up if tagging rules too permissive. Mitigation: conservative default tag set + server-side denylist and sampling enforced by fanout-router.
- Risk: consumer lag in Kafka under burst. Mitigation: set retention and autoscale SLI workers; implement fallback to approximate aggregates when lag > threshold.

Next steps:
1) Finalize fanout-router API and sampling config (this ticket).
2) Create instrumentation PR for runtime (ENG-23412 placeholder).
3) Configure canary in CI infra and schedule canary window (ops runbook).
